reforms.description: The government adopted a five-year plan to improve the quality of R&D and increase public spending on basic research, aiming to enhance the overall research landscape in Japan.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing public spending on basic research is expected to enhance the overall research landscape, leading to higher productivity and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The plan has been adopted and is currently in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform represents a structural, system-wide change in public R&D funding.
reforms.source_quote: In the area of science and technology, the government adopted in July 1996 a five-year plan to improve the quality of R&D and increase public spending on basic research.

reforms.description: The 'New Sunshine Programme' focuses on energy conservation, while the 'Industrial Science and Technology Frontier Programme' emphasizes new materials, biotechnology, and information technologies, aiming to boost R&D in these critical areas.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted R&D in critical areas is expected to drive innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The programmes have been adopted and are currently in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: These initiatives represent significant but narrower reforms aimed at specific sectors.
reforms.source_quote: The 1995 'New Sunshine Programme', for example, focuses on energy conservation, while the 'Industrial Science and Technology Frontier Programme' emphasises new materials, biotechnology and information technologies.
